main_text.head: IOANNIS IACOBI PARETI, PHILOSOPHI ET MEDICI, ad Lectorem
PRAEFATIO,

head.i: In qua Medicinae laus & utilitas breuiter comprehenditur.

main_text.p: QVANTA sit Medicinae praestantia, quamq; honorificè ueteres illi uerè sancti & sapientes homines, de ea iudicarint, uel unus certè Homerus, uates sine dubio rerum humanarum peritiss. abundè testatur, qui hanc artem longè pulcherrimo elogio nobilitauit, inquiens:

p.i: ἰατρὸς γὰρ ἀνὴρ πολλῶν ἀντάξιος ἄλλων.

main_text.p: Hominem enim Medicū, multis alijs hominibus praestare censuit: quod Poeta acerrimi iudicij nunquam dixisset, si nō uidisset, tantum oportere tribui, tam eleganti rerum naturę cognitioni. Quid quòd Homero non tantum uetustiores, sed etiam grauiores uiri, Medicis diuinos honores habuerūt, eosq; beneficentia & studio in numerum deorum sustulerunt? Quod grauiter quidē illi & constanter

page.notes: The Greek line is hard to read on the scan; the word after γάρ ἀνὴρ and πολλῶν is uncertain (the printed form may be ἀντάξιος or αὐτάξιος) and should be checked against Iliad 11.514. The left-hand strip of the scan shows the facing page's margin notes, which are not part of this page. The "4" under the text is a page number, printed beside the asterisk signature "*".
